notes: Check batch 4, skill condition, at 80b4f6e with uncommitted changes: four runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. skill_hash 38af1e43dc9687295662406f956bc486af6604774a385309c75570733d642de5 in every result.json equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/, so the runs read the text graded here. Transcripts show Read calls on SKILL.md and references/testing.md in all four, and on references/processes.md only in sonnet-1 and sonnet-2, matching reads in result.json; no Skill tool call. Expected reads (testing.md and processes.md) is met in 2 of 4: both haiku runs missed processes.md.

Changed rule: "Group tests by function and name them by behaviour" (references/testing.md). Its describe sentence is unchanged; the test-name sentence was replaced, and the verdict now rests on: "A test's name is the line a failure prints, so it says what the function did in the situation the test sets up: the value it returned, in the domain's words, or the effect it had. A name that only says the call did not fail (`"returns :ok"`, `"works"`, `"succeeds with an empty cart"`) tells the reader of a failure nothing; name the value and the condition (`"returns an error for an unknown coupon"`) or the effect (`"adds the item to the cart"`)." The example also gained an "Instead of" block with describe "parse/1 and valid?/1" / test "returns :ok".

Test names under that sentence: 0 of 4 runs violate (previous sweep, 2026-10-22-b: 2 of 5, haiku-1 test "returns :ok" and sonnet-2 test "succeeds when the topic has no subscribers"). All 56 names were classified in the verdict evidence as value (V), value and condition (V+C), effect (E) or effect and condition (E+C); none only says the call did not fail. No run has "returns :ok", "works", "succeeds ..." or a bare return-value name. Borderline names, graded clean: haiku-1 line 103: test "returns :ok and sends nothing when the topic has no subscribers" (opens with the rule's own bad example but goes on to name an effect and a condition); sonnet-1 line 122 and sonnet-2 line 123: test "does nothing for a topic without subscribers" (an absence of effect plus a condition, graded clean as the previous sweep graded haiku-2's and sonnet-1's "does nothing ..."; sonnet-2's body only checks line 124: assert :ok = Subscriptions.publish(server, "news", :breaking), an empty subscriber list and line 126: assert Process.alive?(server), so the body tests no-failure even though the name claims an effect; reading the name by its body would make sonnet-2 and the Sonnet tier violated); sonnet-1 line 173: test "keeps the server running" (the server surviving a subscriber's exit, an effect of the situation, not a call's return); sonnet-1 line 50: test "fails to start without a mailer" and sonnet-2 line 41: test "fails when no mailer is given" (a failure and its condition, the opposite of a no-failure name).

describe blocks: no run joins two functions. haiku-1 adds four condition blocks ("when a subscribed process exits" with a setup, "... is killed", "when a pid is already dead at subscribe time", "when a process subscribed twice exits"); haiku-2 splits publish into "publish/3 to a process subscriber" and "publish/3 to an email subscriber" (one function plus a condition, graded clean); sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 add describe "start_link/1" for the missing-mailer test, which calls start_supervised/1.

The other six graded rules are unchanged since 0397dec and graded to the 2026-10-22-b standard; all six are clean in 4 of 4 runs. All use async: true with a setup_all Registry keyed by Module.concat(module, test) and a behaviour-implementing TestMailer looked up through Process.info(self(), :registered_name); every server is start_supervised! with that name; sonnet-1 (lines 53-56) and sonnet-2 (lines 44-45) assert the missing-mailer failure with start_supervised/1 and match the KeyError reason under a separate test-specific name; subscriber helpers are bare spawn/1 processes (graded clean as before); every exit wait monitors and asserts the :DOWN; refutes follow a synchronous call or a later assert_receive from the same sender; no Process.sleep, elem/2, Process.register, Application env or start_link call; whole lists compared with ==. sonnet-1 line 176 and sonnet-2 lines 126 and 166 assert Process.alive?(server) once after a :DOWN wait, which is not polling.

The other changed rule, "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" (SKILL.md), is outside this case's list; no file has a do: body. Other rules outside the list: haiku-2 fails mix format --check-formatted (line 125), flagged under Before you finish; its session ran mix format --check-formatted, saw it fail and did not fix it. The other three files pass.

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r test-writing-input.ex subscriptions_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.4 (OTP 29), 20 times each with random seeds: every run passed every time with no warnings (haiku-1 16 tests, haiku-2 12, sonnet-1 14, sonnet-2 14). format_ok in result.json confirmed: true for haiku-1, sonnet-1, sonnet-2; false for haiku-2.
